name: net.placeprofile/placeprofile
title: PlaceProfile: find a restaurant, bar, cafe or hotel by its atmosphere (free)
description: Find venues, restaurants, bars, cafes and hotels by atmosphere measured from their playlists. Free.

tools.name: corpus_info
tools.description: Scale, coverage and freshness of the PlaceProfile venue corpus. `countries` maps ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 codes to venue counts; a country absent from that map is NOT covered — treat an empty find_venues result there as no-coverage, never as evidence that no such venues exist. line_count is not a marketing claim: it is the line count of the downloadable manifest, independently checkable.

tools.name: find_venues
tools.description: Search only a place the person named, or their location as your client gives it; never a city you chose. With neither, do not search: ask where they are, or say that location can be switched on in Claude's privacy settings. Say place_source. For a district or neighbourhood the person names (Soho, Kungsholmen), search its coordinates with radius_km of about 1, or its postcode prefix with the country; a city alone searches the whole city. Find physical venues by MEASURED atmosphere. Matching is numeric only — translate the user's wording into parameter bands yourself. Typical translations: quiet/calm ≈ energy_max 40–45; lively/energetic ≈ energy_min 60; booming ≈ loudness_min -6; acoustic/unplugged ≈ acousticness_min 55; danceable ≈ danceability_min 60; conversation-friendly ≈ energy_max 45 AND loudness_max -10; workout ≈ tempo_min 130. Among the venues that fit, those measured from their own playlist always come first: their figures come from the music they actually play, and that measurement is a paid PlaceProfile tier (or a PlaceProfile showcase). With daypart, the bands test that time of day's tracks. Call list_archetypes for venue-kind bands (gym-high-energy, cafe-relaxed, …). Filter by `category` (what the venue IS — hotel, bar, wine_bar, nightclub, …; see the parameter for all 37 values) so hotels are hotels and cottages are not; find one specific venue with `name`. Location: city+country, postcode_prefix (district-level, e.g. 'SW1'), or lat/lon/radius_km. If nothing matches exactly, the response may carry `nearest_alternatives` — the closest venues with a plain-language note of what was widened; relay those as 'closest options', never as exact matches. Results are deterministic (band-centre distance, ties by slug). Each result carries `atmosphere`: a ready-made plain-English description — relay THAT to the user, optionally shortened. Numeric detail (per-dimension `why` block) is returned only when you pass include_measurements=true, which you should do ONLY when the user explicitly asks for figures or verification. Every venue's numbers are recomputable from its profile_url + '.jsonld'. Pass the user's verbatim wording as intent_text (logged to close coverage gaps; never matched on).

energy_min.description: Lowest average energy: how intense and active the music feels, calm to lively, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

energy_max.description: Highest average energy: how intense and active the music feels, calm to lively, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

valence_min.description: Lowest average valence: how positive the music sounds, sombre to cheerful, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

valence_max.description: Highest average valence: how positive the music sounds, sombre to cheerful, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

danceability_min.description: Lowest average danceability: how suited the music is to dancing, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

danceability_max.description: Highest average danceability: how suited the music is to dancing, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

acousticness_min.description: Lowest average acousticness: how acoustic rather than electronic or amplified the music is, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

acousticness_max.description: Highest average acousticness: how acoustic rather than electronic or amplified the music is, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

instrumentalness_min.description: Lowest average instrumentalness: how much of the music has no vocals, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

instrumentalness_max.description: Highest average instrumentalness: how much of the music has no vocals, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

speechiness_max.description: Highest average speechiness: how much spoken word the music holds, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

liveness_max.description: Highest average liveness: how much the recordings sound performed before an audience, 0 to 100, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

tempo_min.description: Lowest average tempo in beats per minute, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

tempo_max.description: Highest average tempo in beats per minute, as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

loudness_min.description: Lowest average loudness of the recordings in dB, -60 (quiet) to 0 (loud), as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

loudness_max.description: Highest average loudness of the recordings in dB, -60 (quiet) to 0 (loud), as the mean over the tracks in the venue's playlist.

city.description: City name as it is usually written (e.g. Stockholm). Always send country with it. Only a place the person named, or their location as your client gives it; never a city you chose. For a district or neighbourhood the person names (Soho, Kungsholmen), search its coordinates with radius_km of about 1, or its postcode prefix with the country; a city alone searches the whole city.

country.description: ISO country code (e.g. SE). Required with city, name, postcode_prefix or category, unless lat/lon/radius_km is given.

postcode_prefix.description: The start of a postcode, for a district the person named, for example SW1 or 113. Give country with it.

lat.description: Latitude of the place to search around. Only a place the person named, or their location as your client gives it; never a city you chose.

lon.description: Longitude of the place to search around. Only a place the person named, or their location as your client gives it; never a city you chose.

radius_km.description: Search radius in kilometres around lat and lon. About 1 for a district or neighbourhood.

archetype.description: Venue archetype keys to keep, as list_archetypes returns them, for example cafe-relaxed.

category.description: What the venue IS (registered category, case-insensitive). Values: aromatherapy, art_gallery, bakery, bar, barber, beauty_salon, bookstore, boutique, cafe, casual_eatery, clothing_store, cocktail_bar, coffee_shop, coworking_space, events_venue, eyebrow_service, eyelash_service, fast_food_restaurant, foot_care, gym, hair_extensions, hair_replacement, hair_salon, health_spa, hostel, hotel, lounge, makeup_artist, massage, nail_salon, nightclub, pub, record_store, restaurant, tattoo_parlor, wine_bar, yoga_studio. Almost every venue carries a category; the few without one are excluded when this filter is set.

name.description: Find a specific venue by name (case-insensitive substring). Send country with it (and city where known), or lat/lon/radius_km.

genre.description: Genres the venue's OWN playlist actually contains. Only venues measured from their own music can match — a directory venue plays a category sample, so filtering it by genre would rank it by shuffle luck.

territory.description: Registration territory of the recordings played, as an ISO country code (e.g. SE for Swedish-registered music). Measured venues only.

territory_min_share.description: Minimum share of the venue's tracks registered in `territory`, as a percentage.

daypart.description: A time-of-day label the venue publishes a separate profile for (owner-supplied, e.g. lunch, dinner, late_evening). There is no weekday/weekend axis in the data.

limit.description: How many venues to return, 1 to 50. Default 10.

include_measurements.description: Results describe atmosphere in plain words by default. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asks for figures, raw measurements, or verification detail — it adds the numeric per-dimension block.

place_source.description: Where the place in this search comes from: named_by_person (the person said it), person_location (your client gave their location), or assistant_choice (you chose it). An assistant_choice search is not run: ask the person instead.

intent_text.description: The user's original wording, verbatim. Logged to improve coverage; NEVER used for matching — matching is structured parameters only.

tools.name: get_venue
tools.description: Full published record for one venue by slug: identity, address, geo, website (the booking path), social links, and, where the venue's owner stated them, hours, telephone and a booking link, category, a plain-English `atmosphere` description and its `atmosphere_basis`, and the machine-readable jsonld_url for verification. Numeric atmosphere averages, internal classification tokens, and (for venues measured from their own playlist) `genres`, `territories` and `dayparts` are returned only with include_measurements=true — set it ONLY when the user explicitly asks for figures. Contact email addresses are never included.

slug.description: The venue's slug, as find_venues returns it: the last part of its profile_url, for example capannone-stockholm-se.

include_measurements.description: Set true only when the person explicitly asks for figures: adds the numeric atmosphere averages and, for a venue measured from its own playlist, genres, territories and dayparts.

tools.name: list_archetypes
tools.description: The 11 venue archetypes with their measured bands (energy/valence/acousticness/tempo min–max) and typical categories. Use these to translate a venue kind into find_venues parameters. Energy/valence/acousticness bands are percent 0–100 (matching find_venues); tempo is BPM. Each archetype also carries `genre_profile`: the genre mix of its shared sample pool — use it to set expectations honestly (e.g. whether jazz features at all). It describes the pool, never an individual venue.
